patch_description: The current ansatz uses a single shared CRZ parameter "d" across all four disjoint pairs [0,1],[2,3],[4,5],[6,7], which forces identical entangling phase for both "even-indexed" and "odd-indexed" pair groups. Splitting this into two shared parameters—d1 for pairs [0,1] & [4,5] and d2 for pairs [2,3] & [6,7]—gives the circuit finer-grained control over correlations between different qubit groups (adjacent-index pairs vs. next-nearest pairs), which can help it adapt to more complex/hard-to-separate data patterns without adding circuit depth. This costs only one extra distinct parameter (5→6), a modest trade-off for potentially much better worst-group margin and validation accuracy, consistent with the pattern seen in the second seed program (6 distinct params, 0.42 score) which outperformed the current single-param version (5 params, 0.41 score, notably worse train accuracy).
